title: Count the Set Bits
statement:
Count how many bits are set to 1 in a 32-bit unsigned value.

## Your function

```
int count_set_bits(unsigned int value);
```

`count_set_bits(0)` is `0`; `count_set_bits(255)` is `8`.

## Watch out

- The argument is `unsigned` on purpose. Right-shifting a *signed* negative
  value is implementation defined, and a loop written around `int` can spin
  forever on a value with the top bit set.
- `value & 1u` tests the lowest bit; `value >>= 1` moves the next one down.
  Stop when the value reaches zero rather than always going round 32 times --
  though 32 times is correct too.
- `value &= value - 1` clears the lowest set bit, which turns the loop into
  one iteration per bit that is actually set.

tests.name: every bit set
tests.description: The largest 32-bit value. A loop built on a signed int tends to hang or come back wrong here.

tests.name: the top bit alone
tests.description: Bit 31 and nothing else -- the value that makes a signed right shift misbehave.
